chunks: What Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad and Muhammad, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abi Hariz Zakariyya ibn Idris al-Qummi, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام about a man who leads people in prayer while they dislike that he recite aloud, 'In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.' He said: 'He should not recite it aloud.'

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلَ عَلَيْهِ السّ: Imam al-Kazim عليه السلام, the authority being asked for the ruling
key_terms.بِبِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: the basmalah, the phrase 'In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful'
key_terms.يَكْرَهُونَ: they dislike or object to a particular practice
key_terms.يُصَلِّي بِقَوْمٍ: leads a group in salat as their prayer leader

ai.seo_question: Should an Imam recite بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ aloud if the congregation dislikes it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the Imam leading congregational salat when the people behind him dislike audible recitation of بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ. The answer indicates that in this circumstance he should not recite it aloud, showing consideration of congregational context in prayer practice.
